With a little more room to think than yesterday, I looked again. The whole castle seemed to be holding itself stiff.

The skin of the soldiers going back and forth was all bristled, and their eyeballs were red from overstretched nerves. The civil officials and ladies-in-waiting were busy with work, but now and then they looked at nothing, shivering a little, as if a cold draft was blowing only for them.

It was too early to let the assassination of Lord General Moriuji fade into the past. Assassination, that is, about eighty percent likely. Its cold rain was plainly falling on all their minds.

This was bad for their health. It was not good for me either.

With vigilance higher than usual, the task given to Ichijou and me became one step harder. Not that carelessness had been in the plan. Still, 'I did not mean to be careless' would be a poor defense afterward. I had to keep a stricter watch. From any side, at any moment, our identity could leak out.

必要があった。いつ何から正体が露顕するか知れない。

en.html:
So the boy carrying a ruler's destiny was now being attended by noble ladies, protected by mighty warriors, and playing with a ball.

It was about the size of a human head, with a black-and-white pattern.

...Soccer, then. Nowhere near the level of its native Europe, but even in Yamato it was gaining popularity. The special feature of the game is that hands are mostly forbidden, and the ball is handled with the feet.

Eleven on one side, eleven on the other, competing for points: that was the proper arrangement. Here, twenty-one players were not in the picture at all. Shirou Kuniuji was kicking the ball up by himself.

It was probably the basic practice called juggling: you keep kicking, and the ball must not touch the ground. As for Shirou Ashikaga's juggling... achchha, let me be polite. It was not good.

In Tokai, where football was most popular in Yamato, two hundred, three hundred touches were nothing unusual for a schoolboy who played. This boy mostly lost his balance and dropped the ball after a few touches, ten or so on a good day. He seemed not to know the knack at all.

His reflexes did not look poor. Someone only had to tell him how. But from these ladies, what instruction was going to come? Kick the ball: "well played." Drop the ball: "magnificent." Same marks for both answers; how was the boy to find the wrong one?

Gend neeche gayi toh bhi wah. Even when the ball went down, praise went up. The boy was attempting football; the audience was playing something else, a game in which His Highness could not lose and therefore could not learn. Only the ball had failed to appreciate the arrangement. That disloyal little sphere continued obeying gravity.

The guard warriors did not even bother with flattery. Probably they were concentrating on duty, but there was also a cold distance in them. Something like a nuisance.

Their faces were behind their helmets, but I could guess the message. If only he would stay indoors, the guarding would be so much easier.

王者の宿命を背負う彼は今、高貴な女達に<ruby>傅<rt>かしず</rt></ruby>かれ、
強剛の武者に守護されながら――<ruby>球<rt>ボール</rt></ruby>で遊んでいる。
　およそ人頭大の、白黒模様の球だった。

　……<ruby>蹴球<rt>サッカー</rt></ruby>か。
　本場欧州とは比べものにならないにせよ、大和でも
人気を獲得しつつある球技である。腕の使用を原則と
して禁じ、足で球を扱う点に特徴がある。

　本来は十一人のチーム二つで得点を争う競技だが、
勿論いま目の前でそれが繰り広げられているという事
はない。
　四郎邦氏は一人で球を蹴り上げて遊んでいる。

　リフティングと呼ばれる基礎練習だろう。
　球を地面に落とさぬよう蹴り続けるものだ……が、
足利四郎のそれは世辞にも上手くなかった。

　大和で最も蹴球が盛んな東海地方の競技少年であれ
ば二百三百とこなすのも珍しくないところ、彼は大抵
数回、良くても十回余りで均衡を失い落としている。
　どうもコツをまるで知らないようだ。

　運動神経は悪くなさそうである。誰かが適切なアド
バイスをすれば伸びるだろう。
　しかし球を蹴ろうが落とそうがお上手です、お見事
ですとしか言わない女達にそれは期待できまい。

　警備の武者らは阿諛すら口にせずにいる。
　任務に集中しているのであろうが――どこか冷たい
よそよそしさもあった。どこか迷惑げな。

　兜に覆われた素顔が覗けるわけではないが、何とは
なし察しはついた。
　屋内に篭もってくれていれば警護も楽なものを――
と言いたいのであろう。

Apparently the boy was not stupid enough to enjoy this praise pasted on like cheap makeup. Nor was he too insensitive to notice the guards' coldness. That face understood both.

Still he went on. Perhaps even this little scrap of playtime was precious. The rest of the time, was he shut behind heavy walls and roofs, exactly as the guards preferred?

His position required it. His rank required it. The present situation required it. For a growing boy, none of those requirements made it less cruel.

That little court noble, keeping up his solitary game with such a stiff face—I found it difficult to watch.

Holding the ball, the princess looked at Kuniuji. What was in her face was not easy to put into words.

Rokuhara was her enemy. Keeping her resentment from showing did not mean it had obediently disappeared.

At the summit of that enemy stood Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga. If the shogunate bore guilt, he could be called responsible for all of it—even though, when the Okabe rebellion happened, he had not yet occupied that position.

Not in all the worlds of the universe could she find a reason to feel anything but hostility toward him.

And yet... she must have seen it also.

In front of her was merely a boy who had been playing, without any other thought. By a strange turn, I had brought that boy out.

Put a blade into her gaze and direct it at him: no blade would come back. It would pass through without resistance. Right into his heart.

Could the surviving princess of Okabe do that?

en.html:
The boy trembled in shock. The daughter of a family destroyed by his Rokuhara, his shogunate army.

She was walking away at an angle, her back partly toward us. Composed, she looked. Not perfectly. A stiffness showed here and there in her movements, as though what she felt inside had reached the edges.

Yoritsuna Okabe's daughter was being led before the shogunate's senior ministers. A pleasant meeting, it could hardly be.

Probably they would question her about what Ms. Iwata had told me: forces opposed to the shogunate, planning to take Sakurako away. Torture, surely they would not go that far. Questioning beyond reasonable limits was another matter.

Here in Fudaraku, she had nobody on her side.

The princess walking away was beautiful. Like one flower, alone, growing in a wasteland.

衝撃を受けた面持ちで、少年が体を震わせた。
　――彼の六波羅、彼の幕軍が滅ぼし去った一族の、
娘。

　彼女はこちらに斜め後姿を見せる格好で離れゆく。
　沈着な様子ではあった。完璧ではなかったけれども。
身ごなしの端々に覗く強張りは、姫の内心そのものに
思えた。

　岡部頼綱の娘が、幕閣の面々の前へ連行されてゆく
のだ。
　心楽しい会合が待つ筈もなかった。

　おそらくは、岩田女史が俺に伝えた事――桜子奪取
を謀る反幕勢力の存在について、査問を行うのだろう。
　まさか拷問には掛けられまいが、度を超した尋問に
なる事は充分に有り得る。

　この普陀楽に、彼女の味方はいないのだから。
　
　去りゆく姫は美しかった。
　荒野にただ一輪で咲く、孤独な花の美しさがあった。
